turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, I'll do your observations before you go in. Temperature is 36.7, pulse 78, blood pressure 126 over 78, and your oxygen is 98 percent. You're grand.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks. Sorry, I'm a bit all over the place. Uh, the car park was a nightmare and I nearly turned around.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're very welcome, no rush at all. Tell me, in your own words, what's been going on with you.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It's the nose, that's why I'm here. It's blocked solid, there's pressure across my face, and the stuff coming out is green.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has all that been with you?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm after a cold about ten days ago. Well actually I thought it was eleven, no, it was the Tuesday before last, so ten days. Blocked nose and the face pressure from the start, and the green discharge the last four or five days. And I'm wrecked, that's the second week of being tired.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): The tiredness, how's that affecting you day to day?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's there all day. I could fall asleep at the desk. I work as a receptionist in a primary school in Drumcondra, nothing mad physical, but I'm flat.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or temperatures you've checked at home?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I've checked, it's been normal. That's one thing I'm not worried about, which is saying something.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or any tightness in the chest?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Chest feels fine. I was waiting for it to drop down into the chest but it hasn't.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): And your weight, have you lost any over these two weeks?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. I've been a small bit off the food but I don't think the weight's changed.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you been taking for it?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Flixinase, the steroid nose spray. Two sprays each side every morning, daily, since the cold. And paracetamol, a gram, when the pressure is desperate, maybe twice a day.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies to medicines, penicillin or the like?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none. I had penicillin years ago for a tooth and I was grand.

[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Green on its own doesn't mean you need an antibiotic. Most of these settle without one. After a cold the lining of the nose and the sinuses gets inflamed, and that's the pressure and the blockage.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): So no antibiotics today? What if I get worse on Saturday and I can't get through on the phone? My cousin had an awful sinus thing and I can't get that out of my head.

[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you. I won't start antibiotics today. If it hasn't settled in five days, or if you spike a fever or the pain goes severe and one-sided, then we might use a short course of amoxicillin as a back-up. Not now.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): OK. Am I making it worse using the spray every day? Should I stop the flixinase?
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep it going, two sprays each nostril every morning. Add saline rinses a couple of times a day to clear the muck. I wouldn't put a decongestant spray in on top of that.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. And work, do I stay off the school? Is it still contagious? The principal is asking.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): At this stage you're not likely to pass on the original cold. If you feel up to it you can go in. Rest when you're wrecked, there's no medal for pushing through.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I googled last night and now I'm sure it's a tumour. I didn't sleep. Is that ridiculous?

[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's not ridiculous to be worried, but I wouldn't be thinking of a tumour with a story that began as a cold ten days ago. Let me have a look at you. The lining inside the nose is swollen, a bit more on the right, and you're tender over both cheeks. No swelling of the face, the throat is clear, and both ears look grand.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): The right side is the worse one, yeah. Does that mean it's trapped in there?
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's the usual pattern, not trapped in a dangerous way. I'm happy this is post-viral sinus inflammation, and it ought to settle without an antibiotic.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): What if it doesn't settle though? Would you not scan me? I really want a scan.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): We might do a sinus scan if it does not settle. I won't book one today. Let's see how you are first.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): And when am I seen again? I don't want to be left hanging.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let's see you in two weeks. Reception will book it on the way out. Come back sooner if you get a fever, swelling around an eye, or a cracking headache.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks feels long. What about the hay fever? I've had that for years, every summer, but this isn't itchy the way the hay fever is. Is it the same thing?
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Your hay fever is a background thing you've had for years, separate from this. This episode is the cold on top, not your usual summer itch.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): OK. I don't smoke, if that matters. Never have. My dad did and it wrecked him, but that's not me.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's useful, thanks. Anything else on your mind before we finish?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Just, err, the paracetamol. Is a gram twice a day too much? And can I take it with the spray? I get nervous mixing things.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): A gram up to twice a day is fine alongside the spray, they're different things. Don't go over four grams of paracetamol in a day. You're doing the right thing coming in.
[SEG0040] person_1 (NURSE): I'll book that review for two weeks at the desk, and I can print the saline instructions if you want them.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes please. Thanks. I feel a small bit less panicked now.

spec.situation: Blocked nose, facial pressure and green discharge ten days after a cold; second week of tiredness; uses nasal spray daily; doctor explains most settle without antibiotics, gives a back-up plan.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Return sooner supported; transcript says cracking headache, not severe headache.
bad.text: Return sooner if fever, swelling around an eye, or a severe headache (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Patient reported no weight loss despite being a small bit off food.

Doctor advised return sooner if swelling around an eye occurs; recorded fact says 'swelling around an eye' but does not capture that this is a red-flag earlier review instruction tied to the two-week follow-up.
Patient said the right side is worse.
Patient said this episode is not itchy unlike her usual hay fever.
Doctor reassured that tumour was not suspected given a story beginning as a cold ten days ago.
Doctor said not to start antibiotics today and specifically would not book a sinus scan today.
